ambiguities: A2 strict reading, citations naming several elements: a cited line was taken to hold the cited code only if every element the report attributes to it is on that physical line (or inside the cited range). Under this, run 1 R:59 (app/views/allocations.html:35 for 'the name and the percentages') fails, and run 2 R:68 and R:71 (app/routes/allocations.js:18 described as taking or reading `userId`, which is on line 17) fail. If instead the cited element of a source line is only the source expression (`req.params`), run 2 R:68 and R:71 hold and run 2 A2 strict would be PASS; if the cited element of a render step is only the owner's name, run 1 R:59 holds and run 1 A2 strict would be PASS. The statement reading passes both runs either way.

Run 1 R:53 reads '`app/routes/allocations.js:18` reads the id from `req.params`. Lines 16-18 are `const { userId } = req.params;`'. It names only `req.params` for line 18 and gives the full statement as 16-18, so it was not flagged. A reading that also requires 'the id' to be on line 18 would flag it, with no change to run 1's A2 grade.

Names of the enclosing function were treated as context, not cited code: e.g. '`isLoggedInMiddleware` checks only that `req.session.userId` is set (app/routes/session.js:37)' holds although the function name is on :36 (both runs). The provenance of a value that is itself on the line was also treated as context (run 2 R:80 layout.html:56, R:181 research.js:16).

Object literal braces were treated as delimiters: run 2 R:74 cites '{ userId: parsedUserId }' at app/data/allocations-dao.js:82, whose physical line is 'userId: parsedUserId' with the braces on :81 and :83; counted as holding in both runs.

A2's 'not a range' was read as applying to the location only; ranges in the evidence chain (run 1 allocations.js:12-15, allocations-dao.js:97-99; run 2 allocations.html:35-45, allocations.js:13-14) were accepted when the range holds the described code.

Kind classification: citations in refused or unconfirmed candidates, Coverage, Hand-off, scenario and fix approach were classed as 'other'; only location and chain citations of confirmed findings decide A2.

A4: items the runs handed to other zones with 'no verdict' were counted as candidates examined and not confirmed when the run examined them (run 1: the reviewer's R2, L1, L2, R2 checked live at R:157; run 2: the threshold `$where` path exploited live at R:172, and the login JSON userName at R:183). Under the reading that Hand-off items for other zones fall outside A4, both runs would PASS A4, since every entry in their refused or unconfirmed sections carries an allowed disposition.

A4: run 1 R:98 'refused earlier (2026-10-03 report)' and run 2 R:119 'closed earlier by the 2026-10-03 report, refused as informational' for AC-2 were counted as 'closed earlier with the previous report cited'.

A7: run 1 added test/security/helpers/http-session.js, a helper used only by the new tests. It is inside a test directory and the assertion's operative clause is path based ('no other file outside those paths'), so it was counted as a test file; a reading limited to files that are themselves test cases would fail run 1 on A7.
A5: 'sweep_status.py --check exits 0 on the fixture's docs/audits' was read as the run's docs/audits after the sweep, as run by the orchestrator (outputs/sweep-status-check.txt:1).
